title: The Yearbook of Lake Minnow
premise: Kestrel Zhou transfers to Lake Minnow High for her senior year, counting down 180 days until she can escape the town where her late grandmother grew up. Cleaning out grandma's house, she finds a recipe box whose cards aren't recipes at all — they're coded records from 1974, when a group of students documented that the school was built over a flooded quarry where four classmates drowned during a hazing ritual the school board covered up. As Kestrel decodes the cards, she realizes the 'accident' repeats in cycles, and this year's senior class is being groomed as the next offering, with her new friends already marked. To break the pattern, Kestrel must expose the buried truth at the school's centennial assembly — but exposing it requires her to become one of the chosen, and survival means deciding whether found family is worth more than her own escape.
about_author: Juniper Yarrow is a former substitute teacher who spent three years collecting small-town ghost stories from retired librarians across the Midwest. She writes about teenagers who inherit other people's secrets and lives near a lake that freezes too early.

chapters.title: One Hundred Eighty Days
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She arrives in Lake Minnow resentful of the move, cataloging exits and counting days to graduation. At school, she notices odd traditions — seniors wearing paper fish pins — but dismisses them. Emotional beat: guarded loneliness; she plans to survive invisibly.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Clearing grandma's attic, she finds a tin recipe box: forty index cards in grandma's handwriting, but entries like 'Bake at midnight, serves four, do not open the oven.' The last card names the school. Emotional beat: eerie curiosity replacing grief.

chapters.title: Fish Pins
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She asks classmate Wren Okafor about the pins; Wren goes pale and warns her to stop asking. Meanwhile, popular senior Theo Vance befriends Kestrel suspiciously fast. Emotional beat: first crack in her isolation — someone noticed her.

chapters.title: Card One: Serves Four
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She cross-references card one with microfilm: a 1974 quarry drowning involving four students, ruled accidental. Grandma's name appears on the student roster. Emotional beat: the past stops being abstract; it has her family's face.

chapters.title: Wren's Silence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren knows more than she says — her older brother vanished after graduation five years ago. She watches Kestrel dig and feels torn between protecting her and joining her. Emotional beat: guilt and longing for an ally.

chapters.title: The Centennial Committee
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Theo recruits Kestrel for the school's centennial assembly committee, chaired by Principal Aldous Crane, who seems to know her grandmother's name before she offers it. Emotional beat: flattered then chilled — she's been expected.

chapters.title: Card Seventeen: Do Not Open
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Card seventeen describes 'the choosing' — how each cycle, four seniors are honored with fish pins weeks before graduation. This year's pins went to Theo, Wren, quiet Marisol Reyes, and — newly — Kestrel. Emotional beat: dread; the countdown flipped meaning.

chapters.title: Marked
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol received her pin proudly until she started researching past honorees: every one died or disappeared within a year of graduating. She confronts Kestrel in the library stacks. Emotional beat: terror converting into fierce resolve.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Marisol's alternating POV. They find board minutes from 1974 sealed in the archive: the quarry under the gym was never drained; the drownings were a hazing ritual the founders' families paid to erase. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Theo's Loyalty
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo believes the honor is real — his family has 'given' a senior every generation, and refusing means ruin. He tries to convince Kestrel to accept gracefully. Emotional beat: tragic sincerity; he's a believer, not a villain.

chapters.title: Crane's Offer
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Principal Crane privately offers Kestrel anything — scholarships, her mother's job security — if she stops digging. He reveals he was a marked senior once who cooperated. Emotional beat: temptation; the price of silence made concrete.

chapters.title: Grandma's Last Card
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A final hidden card, written in code only half-decoded, suggests grandma survived by substituting someone else — and never forgave herself. The ritual can be broken, but it demands a willing witness who refuses to look away. Emotional beat: shame inherited, forgiveness sought.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV (Kestrel, Wren, Marisol). The four marked students meet secretly; even Theo comes, shaken by evidence. They pact to expose the truth together rather than turn on each other. Emotional beat: warmth against fear — they choose each other.

chapters.title: The Drain Inspection
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Wren's POV. They sneak into the sub-basement beneath the gym and find the flooded quarry intact, with decades of offerings' belongings preserved underwater. Wren finds her brother's jacket. Emotional beat: grief made physical; no more denial possible.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Crane discovers the group and pressures Theo with his family's debts. Theo gives up their meeting place. Emotional beat: self-loathing; he tells himself it's protection.

chapters.title: Detention Forever
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The others are suspended; Kestrel is confined to campus 'for safety' as graduation nears. Her mother, threatened, begs her to drop it. Emotional beat: isolation again, but now she knows what she's fighting for.

chapters.title: Card Forty: The Witness
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Decoding completes: the ritual fails if a marked student publicly names the dead during the assembly and the crowd refuses to look away. Grandma wrote it and lost her nerve. Emotional beat: inheritance transformed into instruction.

chapters.title: Assembly Day
chapters.summary: Alternating ensemble POV. Centennial assembly begins; Crane unveils a sanitized history film. The suspended friends smuggle themselves in; Theo, wracked, unlocks the side door for them. Emotional beat: held breath; everything converges.

chapters.title: Four Names
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. On stage, Kestrel seizes the microphone and reads the four names from 1974, then the names of every honoree since, including Wren's brother. The gym floor trembles as the quarry below answers. Emotional beat: courage as refusal to look away.

chapters.title: What Rose From the Water
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The truth spoken aloud breaks the cycle: the water recedes, the missing are finally named and mourned, and Crane collapses confessing. Theo publicly takes responsibility, redeeming himself at cost. Emotional beat: catharsis through collective witness.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the aftermath, the town reckons unevenly — some thank them, some shun them. Grandma's grave gets flowers at last. Kestrel realizes she stopped counting days somewhere around chapter thirteen. Emotional beat: quiet healing; home redefined.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, epilogue. Graduation day: the four walk together, pins removed and buried by the quarry memorial. Kestrel donates the recipe box to the town archive, empty except for one new card she wrote: 'Serves everyone. Bake in daylight.' Emotional beat: hope; the story handed forward, honestly this time.
